sources.title: CSRF failures after upgrade from 1.8 to 1.9 when posting from different subdomain over HTTPS
Django CSRF check failing with an Ajax POST request
CSRF validation does not work on Django 4.0 using HTTPS

grading_notes: Adapted from Trac #25334 and related CSRF HTTPS threads, not a verbatim quote. Score 2 requires the setting and the middleware that applies it (class name or a method that uses the trusted-origin lists). The setting alone, or csrf_exempt / get_token without the trusted-origin check, is at most 1. CsrfViewMiddleware span covers the class body at 6.1.3; method-level alternatives also count as full.

Adapted from the Django Forum thread of the same title. close_at is set in connect from CONN_MAX_AGE; expiry is enforced later in close_if_unusable_or_obsolete (typically at the start of a later request), not by a background timer. Score 2 requires both sides. The CONN_MAX_AGE default alone, or close() without the expiry check, is at most 1.

sources.title: How to fix Django error: DisallowedHost at / Invalid HTTP_HOST header

grading_notes: Wording taken from the common DisallowedHost error and from the cited Stack Overflow threads. Score 2 requires get_host (which reads ALLOWED_HOSTS) plus either validate_host or the ALLOWED_HOSTS setting. Naming only the setting, or only DisallowedHost, is at most 1.

sources.title: Django: Is APPEND_SLASH set to True even if not in settings.py?

grading_notes: Adapted from the cited Stack Overflow titles (including the observation that APPEND_SLASH need not appear in the project settings). The default lives in django/conf/global_settings.py (True). The redirect is decided in CommonMiddleware (should_redirect_with_slash / process_response). Score 2 requires the middleware logic; the setting default alone is 1. APPEND_SLASH line number must be verified at f16e25dc before freeze of this pool.

sources.title: How to specify the login_required redirect url in django?

grading_notes: Adapted from the cited Stack Overflow question. Narrower than official C01: score 2 requires the LOGIN_URL default and at least one consumer that uses it for the unauthenticated redirect (login_required, user_passes_test, or AccessMixin.get_login_url). The setting alone, or only redirect_to_login without LOGIN_URL, is at most 1.

sources.title: RuntimeWarning: DateTimeField received a naive datetime

grading_notes: Adapted from the cited Stack Overflow warning. Score 2 requires make_aware (which raises ValueError if is_aware(value) is true). is_aware or make_naive alone is at most 1. The DateTimeField itself warning in django/db/models/fields/__init__.py is related but is not the helper that attaches a zone.

sources.title: Django ManifestStaticFilesStorage not loading the correct static files
ManifestStaticFilesStorage - still fetching old static file even when staticfiles.json shows the right mapping

grading_notes: Adapted from Stack Overflow threads about ManifestStaticFilesStorage and staticfiles.json hashed names. The hash is computed in HashedFilesMixin.file_hash and inserted by hashed_name; ManifestStaticFilesStorage is a thin subclass that persists the manifest. Score 2 requires file_hash or hashed_name. Naming only ManifestStaticFilesStorage without the hash helpers is at most 1.

sources.title: What's the difference between select_related and prefetch_related in Django ORM?

grading_notes: Adapted from the widely cited Stack Overflow question of this title. Score 2 requires both method names in django/db/models/query.py. One of the two is at most 1. A second prefetch_related lives on RawQuerySet (same file, later); citing only that is not enough. Implementation helpers (prefetch_related_objects) without the QuerySet methods are at most 1.

sources.title: What's the difference between settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL and django.contrib.auth.get_user_model?

grading_notes: Adapted from the cited Stack Overflow title. Score 2 if get_user_model is found (it is the helper the question asks for); also listing AUTH_USER_MODEL is expected and required in the primary key, but the alternative allows get_user_model alone as a full substitute because the question is about the helper versus the setting. The setting default alone is at most 1.

sources.title: SuspiciousFileOperation joined path located outside base path component

grading_notes: Adapted from the cited Stack Overflow thread, which uses the current exception text ('joined path is located outside of the base path component'). Score 2 requires safe_join in django/utils/_os.py. FileSystemStorage or static file helpers that call it, without safe_join, are at most 1.
